role-to-group.statement: In ZPC, roles are always assigned to groups, and all users in a group have the same role.

quotes: In ZPC, roles are always assigned to groups and all users belonging to that group are assigned the same role.

group-model.statement: Each group is assigned a single role and can be assigned to multiple business units; users can belong to multiple groups and switch between them.

quotes: Each group is assigned a single role.
A group can be assigned to multiple business units.
Users can be assigned to multiple groups, so they can perform various tasks based on the group's role and permissions.
Users can switch between groups in the ZPC Admin Portal.

default-groups.statement: The default groups available are Default Super Admin with read, add, edit and delete privileges, and Default Read Only with only read privileges.

quotes: The following default groups are available in the ZPC Admin Portal:
Default Super Admin: A group that has read, add, edit, and delete privileges in the ZPC Admin Portal.
Default Read Only: A group that has only read privileges in the ZPC Admin Portal.

default-group-selection.statement: A user can select a default group after logging in so that the same group is used at the next login.

quotes: You can select the default group after logging into the ZPC Admin Portal. This setting ensures that you are part of the same group when you log back in later.

invalid-group.statement: If an administrator belongs to a group not associated with any business unit, the Administrators and Groups page shows a message indicating the group is invalid.

quotes: If the administrator belongs to a group that is not associated with any business unit, the following message is displayed next to the administrator's name.
This indicates that the group is invalid.

predefined-list.statement: ZPC's predefined roles are Administrator, SecOps, Compliance Auditor, View Only Administrator, IaC Administrator, IaC Developer, IT Administrator, Vulnerability Administrator, Vulnerability Viewer, Kubernetes Onboarding and LocalPlatformAgent.

quotes: - Administrator
- SecOps
- Compliance Auditor
- View Only Administrator
- IaC Administrator
- IaC Developer
- IT Administrator
- Vulnerability Administrator
- Vulnerability Viewer
- Kubernetes Onboarding
- LocalPlatformAgent

default-admin-role.statement: ZPC provides a default admin role with full access to the ZPC Admin Portal, assigned to the default admin and assignable to other admins.

quotes: ZPC provides a default admin role that has full access to the ZPC Admin Portal, and this role is assigned to the default admin, but you can assign this role to other admins as necessary.

view-only.statement: Administrators with a View Only role cannot perform any CRUD operation or export data, and the Actions column and Export icon are hidden for them.

quotes: Administrators with a View Only role cannot perform any create, read, update, and delete (CRUD) operations or export any data. The Actions column in the table and the Export icon across the ZPC Admin Portal are hidden for this role.

matrix-admin-viewonly-secops.statement: In the predefined roles table, Administrator has All modules, sub modules and permissions; View Only Administrator has All modules and sub modules with View Only and Save Investigation permissions; SecOps has All sub modules and permissions on Alerts, Cloud Posture, Investigation and Policies.

quotes: | Administrator | All | All | All |
| View Only Administrator | All | All | View Only Save Investigation |
| Security Operations (SecOps) | Alerts Cloud Posture Investigation Policies | All | All |

matrix-compliance-iac.statement: The predefined roles table has rows for Compliance Auditor (Cloud Posture, Compliance, All), Scheduled Reports (All), IaC Administrator (Administration: Version Control & CI/CD Systems, Workstations & IDEs, All), Policies (IaC Policies, All), Alerts (IaC Alerts, All) and IaC Developer (Administration: Workstations & IDEs, All).

matrix-it-admin.statement: The predefined roles table has rows for IT Administrator (Administration: Scheduled Reports, Integrations, Workstations & IDEs, Version Control & CICD Systems, Single Sign-On, Container Registries & Workloads, Cloud Accounts, Business Unit Management, Audit Logs, All), Role Management (Edit Role, View Role, Export Role) and Analytics (Executive Report, All).

modules-defs.statement: Modules are ZPC features whose data can be filtered by cloud accounts associated with business units, and global modules are those where data is not segregated by cloud account and business units do not apply.

quotes: Global Modules: Data is not segregated by cloud accounts and business units are not applicable for these modules.
Modules: Data can be filtered by cloud accounts that are associated with business units. The business unit filters are applicable for these modules.

modules-list.statement: The ZPC modules table has rows for Cloud Posture (Cloud Assets), Cloud Identity, Compliance, Vulnerability Management, Alerts (Cloud Alerts) and Analytics (Executive Report).

quotes: | Cloud Posture | Cloud Assets |
| Cloud Identity |  |
| Compliance |  |
| Vulnerability Management |  |
| Alerts | Cloud Alerts |
| Analytics | Executive Report |

custom-role-permissions.statement: A custom role has a unique name and, per module or global module, a permission of Access, View Only or None.

quotes: Role Name: Enter a unique name for the custom role.
Access: Select the checkbox for tasks that users can perform in each module or global module.
View Only: Select to provide view-only access to specific modules or global modules.
None: Select to restrict users from accessing or viewing specific modules or global modules.

predefined-immutable.statement: Predefined roles cannot be edited or deleted.

quotes: You cannot edit predefined roles.
You cannot delete predefined roles.

delete-role-in-use.statement: A custom role assigned to a group can be deleted only after another role is assigned to the group.

quotes: If the role is associated with a group, then you need to assign a different role (custom or predefined) to the group and then proceed to delete the role.

delete-group-with-admins.statement: A group that contains administrators can be deleted only after its administrators are moved to other groups.

quotes: If administrators are present in a group, then you need to move the administrators to other groups and then delete the selected group.

admin-self-delete.statement: An administrator can edit their own account but cannot delete it.

quotes: However, while each administrator can edit their account, they cannot delete their own account.

add-groups-first.statement: Zscaler recommends adding groups before administrators because each administrator must be assigned a group.

quotes: Zscaler recommends adding groups before adding administrators, because you must assign a group for each administrator that you create.

reset-password.statement: Choosing Reset Password in the Edit Administrator window sends the administrator an email to reset their password.

quotes: When you click Reset Password, the administrator receives an email to reset their password.

bu-definition.statement: Business units are logical containers for cloud accounts that govern ZPC from a role-based access control (RBAC) perspective, and are mapped to groups that are assigned specific roles and permissions.

quotes: Business units are logical containers for cloud accounts in the ZPC Admin Portal.
Business units govern ZPC from a role-based access control (RBAC) perspective.
Business units are mapped to groups that are assigned with specific roles and permissions.

bu-default-groups.statement: By default the Default Super Admin and Default Read Only groups are assigned to all business units.

quotes: By default, the "Default Super Admin" and "Default Read Only" groups are assigned to all business units.
By default, the "Default Super Admin" and "Default Read Only" predefined groups are assigned to all business units.

bu-add-fields.statement: Adding a business unit takes a Name and the groups to assign it to, and users in those groups can view data and perform tasks on cloud accounts within the business unit.

quotes: Name: Enter a name for the business unit.
Assign To Groups: Select the required groups from the drop-down menu.
Users in the group can view data and perform tasks on cloud accounts within the assigned business units.

bu-delete-moves-accounts.statement: Deleting a business unit that has cloud accounts requires moving them to another business unit; otherwise ZPC moves them to a default business unit.

quotes: If any cloud account is associated with the business unit, then you must move the cloud account to another business unit. Otherwise, ZPC moves the cloud account to a default business unit.

bu-list-columns.statement: The Business Unit Management page lists each business unit with its groups, Account Count (number of cloud accounts) and Created On date.

quotes: Groups: The names of groups assigned to the business unit.
Account Count: The number of cloud accounts in the business unit.
Created On: The date and time when the business unit was created.

bu-edit.statement: Editing a business unit lets you change its Name or select a different group.

quotes: In the Edit Business Unit window, change the Name or select a different Group from the drop-down menu.

key-auth.statement: An API key is required to access ZPC's publicly available APIs, and only the API key is required for authentication before accessing them.

quotes: An API key is required in order to access the publicly available set of Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC) APIs.
Only the API key is required for authentication prior to accessing the publicly available set of ZPC APIs.

key-max-100.statement: A maximum of 100 API keys can be created.

quotes: You can create a maximum of 100 API keys.
Create an API key. You can create a maximum of 100 API keys.

key-shown-once.statement: An API key can only be viewed, copied or downloaded as CSV when it is created and is not available in the ZPC Admin Portal after the window is closed.

quotes: The API key is only available when creating an API key. It is not available to access in the ZPC Admin Portal after you close the window, so store it in a secure location.
Click the View icon to view the API key, click the Copy icon to copy the API key to your Clipboard, or click the Download icon to download the API key as a CSV file.

key-revocation-date.statement: The Revocation Date of a new API key can be Never, 7 Days, 15 Days, 1 Month or 3 Months, and defaults to 7 Days.

quotes: You can set the Revocation date to Never, 7 Days, 15 Days, 1 Month, or 3 Months.
By default, this is set to 7 Days.

key-name-and-role.statement: An API key is created with a name and a group and role, and Zscaler recommends the least permissive role; symbols such as ampersands (&) and asterisks (*) are not supported in the name.

quotes: Name: Enter a name for the key.
Symbols like ampersands (&) and asterisks (*) are not supported.
Role Groups: Select the group and role from the drop-down menu for role-based access.
Zscaler recommends creating an API key with the least permissive role.

key-revoke.statement: Revoked API keys no longer authenticate to the ZPC API but remain in the table, and revoking cannot be undone.

quotes: Revoked API keys no longer allow access to authenticate to the ZPC API, but remain in the table.
Revoking an API key cannot be undone.

key-delete.statement: Deleting an API key cannot be undone; the key is permanently deleted and a new one must be created.

quotes: Deleting an API key cannot be undone. If you delete an API key, that API key is permanently deleted and a new one must be created.

key-status.statement: An API key's Status shows whether it is active, inactive or revoked.

quotes: Status: Indicates whether the key is active, inactive, or revoked.

key-availability.summary: One ZPC page says API keys are always accessible from the page but only displayed at creation; the creating page says the key is not available in the Admin Portal once the window is closed.

positions.says: API keys are always accessible from the page, and only displayed when first created.

quotes: API keys are always accessible from the page and are only displayed when the key is first created.

positions.says: The key is not available to access in the ZPC Admin Portal after the window is closed.

quotes: It is not available to access in the ZPC Admin Portal after you close the window, so store it in a secure location.

key-availability.impact: Store the key when it is created rather than relying on retrieving it from the page later.

super-admin.title: Which role or group "Super Admin" means
super-admin.detail: Trusted IP pages say "Only the Super Admin role"; the predefined roles are Administrator, SecOps and so on, the default groups are Default Super Admin and Default Read Only, and the IdP pages say "Default Super Administrator" and "Default admin". Which one "Super Admin" means is not stated.

role-table-flattened.title: Which permission applies to which module in the predefined roles table
role-table-flattened.detail: The capture prints sub-rows (Administration, Integrations, Analytics, Policies, Alerts) as separate rows under the previous role, and the Permissions column is empty for many sub-rows, so the role-matrix claims say only what the table lists at module level; they leave out the Administrators and Groups and Integrations sub-rows (for example Add Administrator under Compliance Auditor, Delete Administrator and Delete Group under IaC and IT Administrator).

key-inactive.title: What makes an API key inactive rather than revoked
key-inactive.detail: The Status column lists active, inactive or revoked; what makes a key inactive is not stated.
